capitals.name: Gunung Tabur (Berau)
capitals.note: The page names no capital, only 'Istana Gunung Tabur' (the palace, bombed by the Allies in 1945 and rebuilt in 1990 as the Batiwakkal Museum). Coordinates are the researcher's reading of Gunung Tabur on the Berau river, near the Berau seat Sungai Lati.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the Sambaliung row's 1830 outline, 51 cells, 117.26-118.87E and 0.86-2.43N, covers the whole Berau coast and so includes this land). The page: the Gunung Tabur line received 'land north of the Berau River and both banks of the Segah River', with Bulungan to the north, Sambaliung to the west and south and the Sulawesi Sea to the east. It gives no area or boundary, so the shape is a 45 km disc about the palace (about 6,400 km2), an estimate only.

ledger.note: 1810: Berau divides and Gunung Tabur begins. 'Pada tahun 1810, kerajaan Berau terbelah' (the Berau kingdom split in 1810) after a rivalry between the heirs of Aji Pangeran Tua and Aji Pangeran Dipati; 'Sultan Gazi Mahyudi kemudian mendirikan Kesultanan Gunung Tabur'. The page gives the year but no outline, so the land is the researcher's disc.

ledger.note: 1810: Gunung Tabur takes its half of the divided Berau Sultanate: 'the land north of the Berau River and both banks of the Segah River'; Sambaliung took the west and south. The sultanate-of-sambaliung dossier records its half under the same year (the Berau page ends the sultanate in 1810 and says Berau divided in the 13th generation without a year).

ledger.note: 1834: the Dutch conquer Berau and the sultan signs an agreement. The Bulungan page: 'After the Dutch conquered Berau in 1834, they forced the sultan to sign an agreement on 27 September'. The Gunung Tabur page says only that it became a protectorate of the Dutch crown (infobox, undated); the page does not say which of the two Berau sultans signed in 1834, so the date is applied to this half as the successor of Berau.

ledger.note: December 1949: Dutch rule ends. The Dutch East Indies page: infobox 'Dutch-Indonesian Round Table Conference: 27 December 1949'; 'In December 1949 the Netherlands formally recognised Indonesian sovereignty'. The Gunung Tabur page gives no date for the end of the protectorate, so the transfer of sovereignty is used (confidence 2). Pairs the 1834 vassal_start.

The page gives no year for this status, only the sultanate's span 1810-1960: the start is the transfer of sovereignty (page silent). Recorded on the vassal's side, as in the sultanate-of-sambaliung dossier.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch, as the successor named by the sultanate-of-berau dossier (and flagged as needed in the sultanate-of-sambaliung dossier). Three pages opened (id.wikipedia Gunung Tabur, en Bulungan, en Dutch East Indies); no English Gunung Tabur article exists (Sultanate_of_Gunung_Tabur and Gunung_Tabur_Sultanate both returned url_not_found). Unsettled: (1) the outline: the page gives no boundary or area; the shape is a 45 km disc (about 6,400 km2) about the palace, and the real half of Berau was larger; (2) overlap: Cliopatria's Sultanate of Sambaliung row (1830 outline, 51 cells) covers the whole Berau coast and so draws the land of this sultanate too; the Sambaliung dossier carries that outline unchanged, so the two will overlap until the Sambaliung shape is cut; (3) the Dutch dates: 1834 is the Bulungan page's date for the conquest of Berau as a whole, which of the two sultans signed is not given; the end of the protectorate (December 1949) is the Dutch East Indies page's transfer of sovereignty, not a Gunung Tabur sentence; (4) the swapraja status within Indonesia has no date on the page (confidence 1); (5) the cause and exact date of the 1960 end are not given on the page, which only has the header span 1810-1960 and 'dihapuskan'; (6) the year of the split (1810) is the page's own; the Berau page says the sultanate divided without a year; (7) the sultan list is empty in the fetched page, so no rulers are recorded; (8) the palace was bombed by the Allies in 1945 and rebuilt in 1990 (Batiwakkal Museum, opened 1992), not drawn. Gazetteer: none new (coordinates only).
